In corpus linguistics , part-of-speech tagging ( POS tagging , PoS tagging , or POST ), also called grammatical tagging , is the process of marking up a word in a text ( corpus ) as corresponding to a particular part of speech , [ 1 ] based on both its definition and its context .
A simplified form of this is commonly taught to school-age children, in the identification of words as nouns , verbs , adjectives , adverbs , etc.
